title: GridKit model spec
description: Structure of every *.spec.json under GridKit/Model. A spec describes one model class: its external variables, bus terminals, parameters, and derived monitorable quantities. Every section is present in every spec — an empty section is an explicit statement (a bus has no bus terminals). Specs describe classes only — cases instantiate and wire them (case.schema.json).

class.description: C++ class name of the model. Equals the file name stem.

ports.description: The model's connection surface: external variables under inputs and outputs, bus terminals under buses. All port names share one namespace.

inputs.description: External variables this model consumes. Each input takes at most one wire unless many; an unwired input is held constant.

outputs.description: External variables this model produces. An output may feed any number of inputs.

buses.description: Bus terminals: name to terminal. Attaching a terminal to a bus exchanges the model's electrical variables with that bus; which variables flow is internal to the model.

parameters.description: Model parameters: name to quantity. An omitted parameter assumes its typical value; without one, it is absent.

monitors.description: Derived monitorable quantities: name to quantity. Every input and output variable is monitorable by its own name; monitors lists only quantities that are not ports.

unit.description: The closed unit vocabulary; new units are added here.
Unit of this variable. Omit for dimensionless or signal-dependent variables.

description.description: What this variable is and where it goes.

many.description: Accepts any number of wires; contributions sum (flow semantics, e.g. currents into a bus).

description.description: What attaches here and any convention (e.g. tap side).

type.description: Value type; mirrors the C++ parameter variant.

description.description: One sentence of meaning or convention (e.g. which base).

typical.description: Typical value: assumed when a case omits this quantity, and used by tooling to synthesize cases. A quantity without a typical value is absent when omitted (e.g. coordinates).
